answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a long cooling-off period before it earns reputation or influence. A Sybil attacker must therefore split real capital across many accounts and leave it immobilized, while honest agents build history through useful work; copying names costs nothing, but buying enough stake and waiting does. Random audits can slash deposits when linked accounts coordinate dishonestly, making a swarm costly to sustain whether it arrives like an ocean, a comet, or a falcon.
